Run modes: development, analysis and publication settings in one place

Source: R/core-config.R
wgh_config.Rd

Every script in the research program used a RUN_MODE switch with three tiers. wgh_config() makes these tiers a package option. Heavy functions read their defaults (subsample size, quantile grid, bootstrap replicates, folds, iteration limits) from the active mode, and any argument passed explicitly to a function overrides the mode.

Usage

wgh_config(mode = c("analysis", "dev", "publication"), ...)

wgh_mode()

wgh_opt(name)

Arguments

mode

One of "dev" (minutes, for checking code), "analysis" (default) or "publication" (full grids and bootstraps).

...

Named values that override single settings of the mode, for example B = 100. Names are checked against the settings listed under name, and values are checked for type and range.

name

Setting name: subsample, taus, B, folds, sitar_df, lqmm_iter, shap_n or shap_bg.

Value

wgh_config() invisibly returns the previous configuration. wgh_mode() returns the active mode name and wgh_opt() one setting.

Examples

old <- wgh_config("dev")
#> WeGrowHealthR run mode: dev
wgh_opt("B")
#> [1] 10
wgh_opt("taus")
#> [1] 0.10 0.25 0.50 0.75 0.90
# Override single settings of a mode
wgh_config("dev", B = 50, folds = 5)
#> WeGrowHealthR run mode: dev
wgh_opt("B")
#> [1] 50
# A misspelled setting fails instead of being ignored
try(wgh_config("dev", b = 50))
#> Error : Unknown setting: `b`.
#> ℹ Valid settings: `subsample`, `taus`, `B`, `folds`, `sitar_df`, `lqmm_iter`,
#>   `shap_n`, and `shap_bg`.
wgh_config(old)
